title: Release Choreography Canvas — visual ramp & fail-safe editor for gradual releases
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Teams need a way to author, preview, and rehearse progressive rollouts (canary, A/B ramps, burst ramps) without switching between YAML, CLI, and the console timeline. Current flows are fragmented: users either use a text-based editor or a simple percentage slider; neither supports composable safety fences, time-based ramps, or rehearsal mode.

Goal: Design an interactive 'Release Choreography Canvas' — a visual editor where product and platform engineers can compose multiple phases (steady, ramp, hold, burst, experiment), attach safety gates (SLO checks, error-rate thresholds, abort rules), and preview a deterministic timeline and request-sampling simulation. The canvas should produce a config that maps 1:1 to the backend rollout engine (canary + A/B + fallback rules).

Key constraints: must map cleanly to existing rollout policy primitives (percent splits, model variants, region routing). Must support keyboard-first editing and accessible annotations for audits. Must include a deterministic preview (time-series chart + event log) and a one-click 'rehearse' that routes test-traffic to validate guard conditions. Prototype fidelity should be interactive enough for user testing with 6 platform customers.

Approach: Build a two-pane editor: left side a timeline canvas with draggable lane blocks and connectors for transitions; right side a context panel for phase properties and safetyFence presets. Provide inline diffs for proposed rollout vs active rollout and an audit-ready changelog export. Emphasize micro-interactions (snap-to-grid, keyboard nudges, confirmable abort flows).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: multi-tenant RBAC rules for rollout editing (handled in a follow-up), deep metric ingestion UX (we will link to the observability dashboard).
acceptance_criteria: Canvas allows composing at least 4 phase types: steady, linear-ramp, exponential-burst, and experiment (A/B) and persists to rollout JSON
Safety fences can be attached to a phase and accept at least: error-rate threshold, latency P95, and custom metric expression
Preview mode renders a deterministic timeline with simulated traffic distribution per phase and a downloadable event log
Rehearse mode can be triggered from the canvas and shows a simulated run with pass/fail indicators for fences
Visual diff highlights changed phases and shows a clear rollback path (single-click revert to active) in the prototype
Prototype passes remote usability test (N=6 platform engineers) with task success >= 80% for creating a two-phase canary with an abort rule
